newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan government jets raid rebel-held Jalalabad.
newsitem.headline: Afghan government jets raid rebel-held Jalalabad.

text.p: Afghan government jets bombed targets in the rebel-held eastern city of Jalalabad on Sunday, causing at least 25 civilian casualties, a U.N. official said.
The Islamabad-based official said the planes attacked the airport, the governor's palace, the nearby Spinghar Hotel and Behsud Bridge from about 7.45 a.m. (0315 GMT).

He said at least 25 wounded civilians were being treated at one hospital in the city, which was captured in a swift advance by the Islamic Taleban militia on Wednesday. It was not immediately clear if anyone had been killed.
"The raids and anti-aircraft fire created panic in the city," Daniel Bellamy, chief of mission for the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees, told Reuters.
"The streets are deserted and people are sheltering at home," he said, citing reports from U.N. staff on the spot.
Bellamy said eight U.N. international staff of various nationalities remained in Jalalabad, but might be evacuated if the situation there deteriorated.
The Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press said the raid had damaged the ornate 19th-century Bagh-i-Shahi palace built by former Afghan ruler Amir Abdur Rahman beside the Kabul river.
The building's most recent occupant was former provincial governor Haji Abdul Qadir, leader of a group of neutral factions that had previously controlled Nangarhar province.

The Taleban's capture of Jalalabad, astride the main Kabul-Pakistan highway, dealt a major blow to the Kabul government. The rebels are fighting to oust President Burhanuddin Rabbani and install a strict Islamic order.

Afghan sources in Pakistan said on Saturday that government forces had checked the Taleban advance towards the strategic town of Sarobi, about 60 km (37 miles) east of Kabul, and in the border province of Kunar, northeast of Jalalabad.
